# Oil Change Steps? (check my list) 2014 Impreza

Performing an oil change on a Subaru Impreza is less about complex engineering and more about adhering to specific mechanical tolerances that differ significantly from domestic or European counterparts. The core workflow involves draining the sump, swapping the filter, and refilling with synthetic blend or full synthetic oil, but the critical nuances lie in the order of operations and the specific torque requirements for the drain plug.

The first step is accessing the engine bay to loosen the oil filter cap before dropping the vehicle. This prevents a vacuum from forming inside the filter housing, which could make removal difficult once the car is on ramps or jack stands. You must remove the oil fill cap to allow air into the system; otherwise, you risk pulling the new filter onto the old one without draining the sump effectively.

Once the vehicle is lifted using low-profile ramps or a safety jack, move underneath immediately to locate the drain plug. The 2014 Impreza Sport utilizes a standard 17mm wrench for the pan plug. It is crucial to inspect the crush washer before removing the plug. If the washer appears flattened or compromised, replace it with a new one. Do not reuse old washers, as they will lose their sealing ability and lead to leaks.

When draining the oil, have a low-profile catchment pan ready. The engine sits relatively high on the chassis, so ensure your pan has sufficient clearance. As the oil drains, the level will drop below the dipstick tube. Once most of the oil has exited, wipe the drain plug clean and reinstall it. Here is where many DIYers make a mistake: overtightening. The plug should be snug to prevent leaks, but excessive torque can strip the threads in the aluminum oil pan or crack the gasket. A quarter-turn past hand-tight is usually sufficient for the 2014 model year.

Now address the oil filter. Before removing the old filter, carefully wipe the filter mounting pad on the engine block with a lint-free cloth. This ensures no debris falls into the sump when the old filter is twisted off. Regarding the new filter gasket, there is some debate in the community about priming. While some high-performance WRX forums suggest filling the cavity with oil before installation to ensure immediate lubrication upon startup, the factory service instructions for the 2014 Impreza explicitly state only to apply a thin film of fresh oil to the new gasket rim. Do not fill the entire filter cavity unless you are following a specific track-day preparation guide; excessive oil in the filter can lead to foaming if the pump draws it in before the relief valve opens. Install the new filter by hand until the gasket contacts the surface, then tighten an additional three-quarter turn.

After removing the safety jack, refill the engine with 5.1 quarts of 0W-20 synthetic oil. This specific viscosity is required for the direct injection engines found in this generation to ensure proper fuel atomization and reduce friction on internal components. Wait at least ten minutes after filling to allow the oil to settle into the sump before checking the dipstick. If the level is low, add small increments rather than dumping the entire quantity at once.

Finally, reinstall the oil fill cap and run the engine for a few minutes. Listen for any whirring noises coming from the filter housing; this indicates oil is circulating through the new filter. Once the idle sound smooths out, turn off the engine, wait a minute, and perform a final dipstick check before taking the car to the road.
